parts.text: In this experiment, you will investigate the resistance R of a diode using the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) • Close the switch. • Record the voltmeter reading V in the first row of Table 2.1. • Record the ammeter reading I in the first row of Table 2.1. • Open the switch. [1] Table 2.1 resistance between X and Y / Ω V / V I / A R / Ω 10 13 20

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: V and I present and readings to at least 1 d.p for voltage and 2 d.p. for current

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) • Use a spare connecting lead to connect the 3 Ω resistor in series with the 10 Ω resistor between terminals X and Y, as shown in Fig. 2.2. • Record the voltmeter reading V in the second row of Table 2.1. • Record the ammeter reading I in the second row of Table 2.1. • Open the switch. [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Connect the 7 Ω , 10 Ω and 3 Ω resistors in series between X and Y. Repeat the procedure in (b) with this arrangement of resistors. [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate the resistance R of the diode for each pair of readings of V and I from Table 2.1. Use the equation R = V I . Record your answers in Table 2.1. [2]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
all R calculations correct
R values in the range 1.0 Ω to 5.0 Ω inclusive

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) As the resistance between terminals X and Y is increased, the current in the circuit changes. Use your results in Table 2.1 to state the relationship between the current in the circuit and:

ms.label: 2(e)(i)
ms.text: as the current decreases the potential difference / voltage across the diode remains (fairly) constant / decreases (slightly)

ms.label: 2(e)(ii)
ms.text: as the current decreases the resistance increases

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) A student attempts to set up the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1. The student finds that the ammeter does not give a reading when the circuit is complete. The ammeter is not broken. Suggest what the student may have done incorrectly while setting up the circuit. ............................................................................................................................................. [1]

ms.label: 2(f)
ms.text:
diode / power supply / ammeter connected:
the wrong way around / flipped / in the wrong direction
OR
voltmeter connected in series

parts.label: g
parts.text: (g) Name a single device that can be used to control the current in the circuit instead of adding extra resistors in series. Draw the electrical symbol for the device. name of device .................................................................. electrical symbol [1]
